en: The Philippine eagle, known locally as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and one of the largest and rarest eagles in the world.
Emilio Aguinaldo officially declared Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, at his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
Dr. Jose Rizal wrote the influential novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of Spanish friars in the Philippines.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government is a bicameral Congress composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Ifugao people carved the magnificent Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of northern Luzon over two thousand years ago.
During the Pahiyas Festival in Lucban, Quezon, locals decorate their houses with colorful kiping, which are leaf-shaped rice paste decorations.
Baybayin is the ancient pre-colonial writing system where Filipinos used characters made of dots and lines to write on bamboo.
Dr. Fe del Mundo, the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School, invented an improvised bamboo incubator for rural Philippine hospitals.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his massive canvas Spoliarium.
Pagmamano is a traditional Filipino gesture of respect where a younger person presses the back of an elder's hand to their forehead.
The Philippine Constitution guarantees the right of all children to receive free public basic education from elementary through high school.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a spectacular eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
